title: Which Optimizer Leaks Most? Optimizer Implicit Bias as a Training-Data Privacy Controller
abstract: arXiv:2610.18294v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Releasing a neural network checkpoint can leak information about its training data, and existing reconstruction results rely on gradient-descent training. We ask whether the choice of optimizer affects the ability to recover the training data. Extending work connecting Karush--Kuhn--Tucker conditions to training-data reconstruction, we show that the implicit biases of popular optimizers (SGD, Adam, Muon) leave very different fingerprints of the training data. We argue that the key distinction is the \emph{weight-specificity} of these implicit biases, namely how much continuous information about the final weights the optimizer-dependent target of the stationarity conditions encodes. The limiting stationarity conditions for models trained with SGD and Muon retain enough weight-specific information to reconstruct training examples in practice. tldr: 该研究揭示了不同优化器（SGD、Adam、Muon）的隐式偏置在训练数据上留下不同强度的“指纹”，其权重特异性决定了训练数据泄露程度，从而提出优化器的选择本身可以作为一种控制神经网络训练数据隐私的机制。
en_tdlr: This study shows that the implicit biases of popular optimizers (SGD, Adam, Muon) leave distinct fingerprints on training data, whose weight-specificity determines the degree of training-data leakage, thereby proposing that the choice of optimizer itself can serve as a privacy controller for neural network training data.
